Each snake species produces a distinct cocktail of toxins that attack nerves, blood, or tissues, making it difficult to develop a unified treatment. IISc researchers and collaborators at the Technical University of Denmark have developed a recombinant, nanobody-based antivenom that offers broad protection against venom from geographically diverse cobra and king cobra species in India. These recombinant antibodies can be manufactured using microbial and humanised expression systems without repeatedly immunising animals like horses. Additional antibody components can be added to expand protection to other medically important snakes, allowing future recombinant antivenoms to be tailored for different regions or species. Read: https://www.iisc.ac.in/events/engineered-antibodies-offer-broad-protection-against-deadly-cobra-toxins/ #IIScresearch
